title: Transforming JSON
summary: Map a backend's shape to your public contract, and pick the right tool: jq, JSONPath, Simple, a script or code.

steps.title: Why transform at all?
body: Your public contract should not be a copy of a backend. Transforming lets you:
- **survive backend changes**: when the backend renames a field, only the mapping changes.
It is the integration's version of mapping an entity to a DTO. In Camel the usual tool is **jq**:
A field not listed (`internalCost`) simply disappears.

steps.prompt: The backend returns `{"isbn":"1","title":"Refactoring","stock":{"north":3,"south":0},"internalCost":9}`. What does the jq expression `{isbn, title, inStock: (.stock.north + .stock.south > 0)}` produce?
options: An error, because `internalCost` is not mentioned
steps.explain: `{isbn, title}` is jq shorthand for `{isbn: .isbn, title: .title}`. Only listed keys appear in the result.

steps.title: Choosing the tool
body: | **jq** | reshaping JSON → JSON in one declarative expression | another small language to learn |
| **JSONPath** | *extracting* a value for routing or splitting: `$.lines[*].isbn` | not for building new documents |
| **Simple** template | tiny bodies, `{"status":"ok"}` | easy to produce **invalid JSON** (quotes, escaping) |
| **Constant** | fixed bodies and header values | nothing varies |
| **JSONata** / mapping file | rich mappings kept in their own file | one more file type to review |
| **Groovy / JavaScript** script | logic too awkward for jq | logic hides inside scripts |
| **Java bean / processor** | complex, tested mappings with lookups | compiled code; needs a developer |
| **unmarshal → objects → marshal** | when you already have typed classes | verbose for simple reshaping |

items: Map 40 fields with currency conversion from a rates table, with unit tests
Turn an array of backend items into an array of `{isbn, qty}`

steps.prompt: A route builds its body with Simple: `{"title":"${variable.title}"}`. The title is `The "Clean" Coder`. What happens?
options: The body becomes invalid JSON, because the quotes inside the title are not escaped
Camel rejects the exchange before sending
steps.explain: String templates don't know they are producing JSON. Use a JSON-aware tool (jq, a serializer) whenever values come from data.

steps.prompt: Complete the jq expression: produce an array of `{isbn, quantity}` from the backend's `items`, renaming `qty`.
steps.explain: `.items[]` iterates over the array; the surrounding `[ ... ]` collects the results back into an array.
`JsonObject` keeps insertion order, and `decimal` keeps the price exact. `internalCost` was never copied.

steps.title: Map a book to the public contract
prompt: Write `string ToPublicBook(string backendJson)` using `System.Text.Json`. The backend returns:
Return compact JSON with exactly these properties, in this order:
- `author` = first and last name joined by a space, **trimmed** (either part may be missing);
- `tags` = the backend's tags, or an empty array if missing;
- never include `internalCost` or any other field.
hints: `JsonNode.Parse(json)!.AsObject()` gives you a dictionary-like object; `b["x"]` is `null` when missing.
Build a new `JsonObject` in the required order and return `ToJsonString()`.
template: Dojo.Check("internalCost never appears", !ToPublicBook("{\"isbn\":\"2\",\"title\":\"x\",\"priceCents\":1,\"internalCost\":5,\"supplier\":\"s\"}").Contains("internal"), "an internal field leaked");
